# Prospective equal-budget weighted set-cover challenge

Frozen before solving any of the 20 held-out matrices. Use every NRE, NRF, NRG and NRH instance 1–5 from Beasley's [OR-Library release](https://people.brunel.ac.uk/~mastjjb/jeb/orlib/scpinfo.html). These four 1990 families were absent from the earlier 45-instance comparison. Do not read best-known costs for fitting or early stopping. Each method receives the matrix and costs with identical coverage constraints. Supply a common cost-per-new-row greedy cover with reverse deletion. Charge all method-specific work after this shared initialization to a five-second single-thread process-CPU allowance. Credit only feasible witnesses recorded by that deadline. Exclude parsing and the shared warm start. Pin one logical CPU per worker and use seeds 11, 29 and 47.

The candidate perturbs the current cover by dropping random selected columns, repairs the uncovered rows by cost-sensitive greedy insertion, and removes redundant columns. For each repair choose a random uncovered row, rank its incident columns by newly covered rows per unit cost with a small independent multiplicative perturbation, and keep the best. Drop size varies uniformly from 1 to about one third of the current cover; occasionally restart from the best cover. Compare against the common greedy warm start, the original one-drop exchange, a same-code one-drop ablation, Zhu's SetCoverPy with its published defaults (retain completed greedy incumbents), HiGHS mixed integer programming with a warm start, and the Accorsi–Cavaliere implementation of Caprara–Fischetti–Toth with a warm start. Give each solver the full budget and record feasible incumbents at its natural public update points; solver setup and witness monitoring are charged. When an incumbent is already optimal the margin can be impossible.

For each method and instance take the median cost over seeds; deterministic methods need one execution. Primary estimand is the equally weighted mean across instances of the relative cost saving (baseline minus candidate) / baseline. The four families each contribute five instances. A comparison passes when mean saving is at least 1%, its two-sided 95% family-stratified paired instance-bootstrap lower endpoint is positive, and its one-sided paired sign-flip p-value (enumerating all signs for at most 20 differences, Holm-adjusted across all comparisons) is below .05. The sign-flip test assumes exchangeability of paired signs under the null; the finite library supplies a restricted scope. Report every comparison, per-family effects and seed witnesses. A failure against one baseline keeps this study outside the strict portfolio count.

CFT is a directly relevant specialist control from Operations Research. Zhu is a published Lagrangian implementation already used in the earlier study. The MIP solver and same-code ablation control solver class and neighborhood size. Passing this registered challenge would still require a novelty and coverage review for any broader claim. [CFT paper](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.47.5.730) · [CFT implementation](https://github.com/c4v4/cft/tree/6cb63d0036223b8be9c4d01f95b296d641209f95) · [SetCoverPy](https://github.com/guangtunbenzhu/SetCoverPy/tree/a1ff3c5cec45cc1b16541999a4adb593fa652363) · [HiGHS](https://github.com/ERGO-Code/HiGHS)
